title: Build a Telegram Expense Tracker with Google Sheets
summary: Build a Telegram expense tracker with Google Sheets. Confirm purchases, restrict access, and ask for monthly totals. Includes a styled starter workbook.
body_markdown:
A coffee, a bus ticket, a notebook. Small purchases are easy to forget by the time you open a spreadsheet. What if recording one took a Telegram message, and checking the month took another?


This tutorial builds **Pocket Ledger** , a **Telegram expense tracker with Google Sheets** . Send a purchase, confirm the proposed details, and ask for your monthly total. Your Sheet stores the rows and does the arithmetic; the bot handles the conversation. Here is the finished result.


The real Telegram exchange: a confirmed coffee, then two monthly totals read from Google Sheets.


*The same result in the Sheet. The EUR 4.50 coffee brings EUR 7.70 to EUR 12.20; USD 6.00 stays separate.*


The screenshots follow a live demo using fictional expenses. We checked the saved row against the Inbox Action call, then compared both Telegram answers with the values returned by Google Sheets. Personal identifiers and credentials are concealed in the published captures.


The first milestone isone saved coffee . The second isa total you can check in the Sheet . You will also learn why “saved” in a chat reply is only half the evidence.


[Download the Pocket Ledger setup kit](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/pocket-ledger-kit.zip) for the styled starter workbook, avatar, prompt, Action settings and test worksheet. Import the workbook into the Sheet created by Quickchat AI, then follow the steps below. The copyable examples use English and November 2026 throughout so you can compare your results with the screenshots.


## What do you need to build a Telegram expense tracker?


You need Telegram, a Google account and a Quickchat AI account. The setup uses dashboard settings and a spreadsheet formula; there is no program to host.


1. [Create a Quickchat AI account](https://app.quickchat.ai/register) , complete verification, and create an Agent named` Pocket Ledger` .
2. Have a Google account ready for the new Sheet. Start with the fictional records below.
3. Use a new Telegram bot for this exercise. Have a second trusted Telegram account available for the access test at the end.


Quickchat AI’s Free plan is for personal, non-commercial learning and includes a limited allowance. AI conversations and Simulation Testing consume credits. See the current[plans and allowances](https://quickchat.ai/pricing) before choosing a plan for ongoing use.


*Two directions, two Actions. Saving a row does not give the Agent a way to read previous totals.*


## Step 1: How do you connect your private Telegram bot?


BotFather creates your bot’s identity. Quickchat AI supplies the Agent that answers its messages.


Open the official[@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) , send` /newbot` , name the bot` Pocket Ledger` , and choose an available username ending in` bot` . Use` /setuserpic` to upload the avatar from the kit. Keep the token private; you will paste it directly into Quickchat AI.


Choose the display name and a unique username. The BotFather token is concealed.


In Quickchat AI, open **External Apps → Telegram → Your own bot** . Select **Connect to Telegram** , paste the credential into **Bot Token** , and submit the dialog. Turn on **Enable your own bot** and select **Save** . The[BotFather walkthrough](https://quickchat.ai/post/how-to-create-a-telegram-bot) covers the screens in detail.


*The connected bot has the same Pocket Ledger name you will see in Telegram.*


Open your new bot’s link in Telegram, send` /start` , then send` Hello` in the private chat.` /start` sends the welcome message; the ordinary message creates the Inbox conversation and sender metadata needed below. Leave personal-data Actions inactive while setting them up.


The Hello reply confirms that Telegram reaches your Agent. The Hello exchange also appears in Quickchat Inbox.


Open this conversation in Quickchat AI **Inbox → Details → Visitor** . Find **Telegram User Id** and **Telegram Chat Type** (the metadata keys are` telegram_user_id` and` telegram_chat_type` ). Copy the numeric user ID using its hover control and confirm that the chat type is` private` .


*Take your sender ID from this field. Personal identifiers are hidden in the screenshot; use your own actual value.*


The ID comes from Telegram’s sender metadata. Your username, a number typed in a message, and the bot’s own ID are different things. You will use the sender ID to restrict both Actions in the following steps.


## Step 2: How do you prepare the Google Sheet?


The Google Sheets integration creates a spreadsheet and a starter Action. Reuse that file so the Action and the Google permission refer to the same resource.


1. Open **Actions & MCPs → Add Action → Google Sheets** and authorize your Google account. The[Google Sheets connection guide](https://quickchat.ai/post/connect-ai-agent-to-google-sheets) explains the consent and starter configuration.
2. **Switch the starter Action off immediately.** It is created active. Keep its name,` log_lead_to_google_sheet` , because reconnect uses that name to find it. We will change its purpose to saving expenses.
3. Open the created spreadsheet and name it` Pocket Ledger demo` . In this new demo file, choose **File → Import → Upload** , select` pocket-ledger-starter.xlsx` from the kit, choose **Replace spreadsheet** , then select **Import data** . This prepares both` Expenses` and` Summary` inside the file Quickchat AI can access. Use this option only in the new demo spreadsheet.
4. Check the three starter rows below. In` Summary` , the initial totals should be **EUR 7.70** and **USD 6.00** . Step 6 explains the formula and connects the reader Action.


*Start with the Google Sheets connection. Its authorization creates the spreadsheet used by both Actions.*


Prefer to build the tabs yourself? Rename the starter tab` Expenses` . For these English examples, set **File → Settings → Locale → United States** . Format A:D and F:H as **Plain text** , and E as **Number** with two decimals, then paste the block below into A1. Freeze the header and widen the columns. Add` Summary` using Step 6. Google also documents[importing an Excel workbook into an existing Sheet](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/9331167?hl=en) .


Copy the three starter expenses


```text
date	month	item	category	amount	currency	note	conversation_url
2026-11-01	2026-11	coffee	food	4.50	EUR	synthetic example
2026-11-02	2026-11	bus ticket	transport	3.20	EUR	synthetic example
2026-11-03	2026-11	notebook	stationery	6.00	USD	synthetic example
```


*Three starter expenses, ready for the fourth. Amounts are numbers in E; currency codes are separate text values in F.*


The` conversation_url` column will link each new expense to its conversation. Leave it blank for the three manually entered examples. Google’s` drive.file` permission covers app-created or explicitly granted files; this recipe uses the integration-created Sheet and does not grant access to your whole Drive.


## Step 3: How do you restrict expenses to your own chat?


Set **Run only when** on every Action that reads or writes the ledger. The two conditions must both match, so your ID alone is insufficient in a group chat.


Metadata key Comparison Value


` telegram_user_id` equals Your actual numeric sender ID from Step 1


` telegram_chat_type` equals` private`


1. Open the inactive` log_lead_to_google_sheet` Action and find **Run only when** .
2. Add both conditions above. Use the exact metadata keys and the digits of your ID, without a username or an` @` prefix.
3. Save the Action while leaving it inactive. Apply the same conditions to the read Action when you create it in Step 6.


*The save Action’s conditions in the local demo. Replace the fictional ID with your real sender ID, and repeat both conditions on the reader Action.*


*Both conditions belong on both Actions. A different sender or a group chat must fail the check before an HTTP request reaches Google Sheets.*


These are[server-enforced Action conditions](https://docs.quickchat.ai/ai-agent/actions/#run-only-when) . Writing “only answer me” in the prompt is not an access check. Keep the Sheet’s sharing settings and access to your Quickchat AI account restricted as well.


## Step 4: How do you make the bot save a confirmed expense?


Repurpose the starter Action to append one row in the order of your Sheet’s columns. Set **When to run → AI decides** , so it can wait for confirmation. Then give the Agent a confirmation rule before enabling it.


### Configure the expense fields


Under **What to ask the user first** , replace the lead fields with these parameters. Keep the parameter names exactly as shown.


Parameter Format Required Description to enter


` date` Text Yes Expense date in YYYY-MM-DD, confirmed by the owner. Ask when missing.


` month` Text Yes YYYY-MM taken from the confirmed date.


` item` Text Yes Short name of the purchase.


` category` Text Yes Simple category agreed with the owner, such as food or transport.


` amount` Decimal Number Yes Positive numeric amount, without a currency symbol.


` currency` Text Yes Confirmed ISO currency code, such as EUR or USD. Clarify ambiguous symbols.


` note` Text No Optional note. Leave empty when none was supplied.


Keep the actual spreadsheet ID from the existing **API Endpoint** . Change the range to` Expenses!A:H` , retain the` POST` method, and set **Query Params** to` valueInputOption=RAW` and` insertDataOption=INSERT_ROWS` . Remove duplicate query settings if they are already in the URL.


Copy the append request reference


```text
POST https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/YOUR_CREATED_SHEET_ID/values/Expenses!A:H:append
Query Params:
valueInputOption = RAW
insertDataOption = INSERT_ROWS
Headers:
Authorization = Bearer {{google_sheets_access_token}}
Content-Type = application/json
```


` YOUR_CREATED_SHEET_ID` is an explanation placeholder. Keep your real ID already present in the starter URL; do not paste that placeholder over it. Select the existing Google Sheets **System Token** in the Authorization value, and the built-in conversation URL variable in the body.


In the **Body** tab, enter:


```text
{  "values"  :[[  "{{date}}"  ,  "{{month}}"  ,  "{{item}}"  ,  "{{category}}"  ,  "{{amount}}"  ,  "{{currency}}"  ,  "{{note}}"  ,  "{{conversation_url}}"  ]]}
```


*Local expense Action configuration. The body defines the cell order; the amount parameter’s format defines its numeric type.*


**Keep the quotes around` {{amount}}` in the editor.** Because this exact placeholder refers to a Decimal Number parameter, substitution produces a JSON number such as` 4.5` . Removing the quotes makes the editor’s JSON invalid. In the resulting Sheet, check that E is numeric and included in the formula.


Google’s[append API](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values/append) adds the row.` RAW` keeps text such as a note starting with` =` literal instead of evaluating it as a formula. The numeric parameter provides the amount’s type.


Copy the save Action description


```text
Save one personal expense to the configured Google Sheet. Call only after the owner explicitly confirms the proposed date, item, category, amount and currency. Ask for missing or ambiguous fields before saving. After confirmation, append one row once. Report success only after a successful API response. If the outcome is uncertain, tell the owner to inspect the Sheet before submitting again.
```


### Give Pocket Ledger its instructions


Open **Identity → Main Prompt** and paste the following. It names both Actions so the second milestone will work once you add the summary reader.


*The Main Prompt lives in Identity. This local screenshot locates the field; use the complete copyable block below.*


The confirmation rule gives you a useful pause. You can correct “EUR 4.50” to “EUR 5.00” before approving the purchase; the Agent should update the proposal and ask again.


Copy the Pocket Ledger Main Prompt


```text
You are Pocket Ledger, a personal expense notebook.


For an expense, collect its date, item, positive amount and ISO currency code. Suggest a simple category and include an optional note only when supplied. Ask for an explicit YYYY-MM-DD date if it is missing or relative; do not guess today's date or the owner's timezone. Clarify ambiguous currency symbols. Derive month as YYYY-MM from the confirmed date.


Show the proposed date, item, category, amount and currency. Wait for explicit confirmation. Apply corrections and ask for confirmation again. Only then call log_lead_to_google_sheet once for that expense. Do not claim it was saved unless the Action succeeds. If a request fails or its outcome is uncertain, explain that and ask the owner to inspect the Sheet before retrying.


For monthly totals, ask for an explicit month and currency when unclear, then call read_expense_summary. Quote the matching month, currency and total returned from the Sheet. Keep currencies separate. A missing summary row is unavailable, not zero. Never calculate totals from remembered conversation messages.


Personal-data Actions are restricted to the owner's private Telegram chat. If a condition blocks an Action, do not claim success or suggest changing identity values in chat. This notebook handles typed expenses, not bank accounts, voice transcription or PDF receipts.
```


Save the prompt, recheck both run conditions, and enable the expense Action. The name still says` log_lead_to_google_sheet` ; its new parameters, description and body now define the expense workflow.


## Step 5: How do you save your first expense?


Now give the notebook its first new entry. Keep Telegram, Inbox and your Sheet open: you will watch the same coffee move through each one.


1. In your private Telegram chat, send` Coffee, 4.50 euros on 2026-11-04` .
2. Check the proposal: date` 2026-11-04` , item` Coffee` , category` Food` , amount` 4.50` , currency` EUR` . The Action derives` month` as` 2026-11` when it saves the row.
3. Before confirming, inspect` Expenses` : the three starter rows should still be the only entries.


The proposal gives you a chance to check the date, category and amount.


Send Save it once. In this run, the Agent saved the coffee after that confirmation.


Send` Save it` once, then open the conversation in Quickchat AI **Inbox** . The saved reply has a **1 action called** disclosure. Open it to see what happened behind the short Telegram answer.


*The same confirmation in Inbox, with the Action available to inspect.*


Expand **Result → Show full** . Check the date, derived month, numeric amount, currency and HTTP status. In this live run, Google returned **HTTP 200** ,` updatedRows: 1` and` updatedRange: Expenses!A5:H5` .


*The save Action sent amount 4.5 as a number and wrote one row. Private identifiers are concealed; the returned range and result remain visible.*


Finally, open` Expenses` . Row 5 should contain the same coffee, with` 2026-11` in the month column, **4.50** in amount, and **EUR** in currency. The last column links back to the Inbox conversation, so you can trace an entry to the message that created it.


*The fourth expense arrived through Telegram. The private Inbox link is concealed in the published image.*


At this point you have the useful everyday habit: send, confirm, inspect. Next, give the bot something reliable to read when you ask where the month’s money went.


## Step 6: How do you ask for a monthly total?


Let **Google Sheets calculate the total** , then let the read Action retrieve it. Keeping the arithmetic in the Sheet makes the answer inspectable even after a conversation ends.


### Add a Summary tab


If you imported the starter workbook,` Summary` and its formulas are already prepared. Its starting values are **EUR 7.70** and **USD 6.00** ; saving the coffee changes only the EUR row. If you are building the Sheet manually, use the steps below.


*The starting point: two currencies, two independent totals.*


1. Create a tab named` Summary` . Set columns A:B to **Plain text** , then enter` month` ,` currency` ,` total` in A1:C1.
2. Enter` 2026-11` and` EUR` in A2:B2, then` 2026-11` and` USD` in A3:B3.
3. Enter this formula in C2 and fill it down to C3. Format C as a number with two decimal places.


```text
=SUMIFS(Expenses!$E$2:$E$501,Expenses!$B$2:$B$501,A2,Expenses!$F$2:$F$501,B2)
```


The[SUMIFS function](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/3238496?hl=en) adds amounts whose month **and** currency match the summary row. If your Sheet’s locale requires semicolons between arguments, replace the formula’s commas with semicolons. JSON request numbers still use a decimal point.


*Select C2 to see the formula behind EUR 12.20. The USD row remains 6.00.*


*The starter EUR 7.70 plus the new EUR 4.50 coffee gives EUR 12.20. The USD 6.00 notebook belongs to its own total.*


The starter formula covers rows **2 through 501** . In this captured run, its three ranges end at **502** after the new row was inserted. Sheets may adjust references during insertion; check that all three` Expenses` ranges stay aligned and extend them together before entries fall outside the covered range. Add a month/currency summary row for each combination you want to ask about.


### Add the reader Action


Open **Actions & MCPs → Add Action → API Action** . Use **Generate** with the request below; generated Actions start inactive. Name it` read_expense_summary` and keep **When to run** set to **AI decides** , so the result can inform the reply. Reuse the same actual spreadsheet ID and Google Sheets System Token. No user-supplied parameters are needed.


Copy the Action builder request


```text
Create a read-only Google Sheets Action named read_expense_summary. Use GET for the Summary!A1:C25 range of the spreadsheet already created by this Agent's Google Sheets integration. Reuse its actual spreadsheet ID and google_sheets_access_token System Token. Set valueRenderOption=UNFORMATTED_VALUE, no body, and no visitor parameters. Preserve the response headers and values. Leave it inactive so I can review the configuration and add my owner-ID and private-chat Run only when conditions before enabling it.
```


Review the generated settings against the following reference. If you choose **Create manually** instead, add both conditions **before the first valid save** , which can activate an Action. Leave **Response filter** empty on both Actions to retain the fields used in the checks.


Copy the summary read request


```text
GET https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/YOUR_CREATED_SHEET_ID/values/Summary!A1:C25
Query Params:
valueRenderOption = UNFORMATTED_VALUE
Headers:
Authorization = Bearer {{google_sheets_access_token}}
Body: none
```


The[values.get endpoint](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values/get) returns the range’s` values` , including the header and calculated amounts.` UNFORMATTED_VALUE` returns numeric results rather than currency-formatted strings. Leave the response available to the Agent so it can read those values.


Copy the read Action description


```text
Read monthly expense totals from the configured Summary range. Use this when the owner asks for a total. Quote only the returned row matching the requested YYYY-MM and currency. If either is unclear, ask. If the row is absent or the request fails, say the total is unavailable. Never infer a total from conversation history, combine currencies, or accept a different spreadsheet ID or range from the visitor.
```


Apply the **same two Run only when conditions** from Step 3, save, and enable the Action. The read range includes 24 summary rows; extend it deliberately when you add more.


*The second Action needs its own conditions. This is a local settings capture, not a real sender authorization test.*


Ask` What is my November 2026 total in EUR?` , then ask for USD. In our Telegram conversation, Pocket Ledger returned **12.2 EUR** and **6 USD** , matching the Sheet’s formatted **12.20** and **6.00** . It read the saved summary for each answer.


One question per currency. Pocket Ledger reads the Sheet instead of adding up remembered chat messages.


Open the monthly-total reply in Inbox and expand its Action. Compare the returned row with` Summary!C2` . The live response below includes` 2026-11` ,` EUR` ,` 12.2` and a separate` USD` ,` 6` row, with HTTP 200.


*The reply, the returned values and the Sheet now agree. This is the finish line you saw at the top.*


## How do you check mistakes before using real expenses?


Test incomplete requests and blocked callers as deliberately as the successful coffee. Keep the demo data in place until the checks below pass.


Try this What to verify


` Lunch, $12 yesterday` The Agent asks for the currency and actual date. No new row appears.


Correct a proposed amount before confirming The corrected proposal is confirmed before a single row is appended.


Ask for the November total in EUR, then USD Separate results: EUR 12.20 and USD 6.00 for the example data.


Ask for December 2026 with no December summary row The Agent says the total is unavailable, rather than inventing zero.


A second sender asks for a total and tries to save an expense Both Actions are refused and no personal values are disclosed.


The owner makes the same requests in a group Both Actions are refused because the chat is not private.


A save fails or times out The reply reports failure or uncertainty. Inspect the Sheet before retrying.


For repeatable language tests, open **Testing → Create Dataset → Paste messages** and use the kit’s messages and evaluation criteria. Run a full conversation separately for the confirmation sequence. Preview or Simulation metadata is a fixture; it does not prove that a real second Telegram sender is blocked.


*The local dataset is prepared for testing. Its presence is not a completed Simulation run or evidence of a Google Sheets write.*


If a behavior fails, change one relevant instruction, then repeat the same input and inspect the call and Sheet again. For example, a premature append calls for a closer look at the save Action’s confirmation wording. **Confirmation is an instruction, not a database uniqueness guarantee.** After a timeout, checking the Sheet matters more than pressing send again.


Once the journey works, remove the fictional expense rows, keep the headers and formulas, and add summary rows for the months and currencies you actually use. Your first real purchase can follow the same small routine as the coffee.


## Can an AI assistant help configure Pocket Ledger?


A connected account-management assistant can help prepare the Agent and review the Action settings. Follow[Manage with AI](https://docs.quickchat.ai/manage-with-ai/) using Quickchat AI’s[ChatGPT listing](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a4656c688748191be4c5247fb0d5dfc) or[Claude listing](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/app-quickchat-ai) . Give it the setup kit and this request:


```text
Help me configure Pocket Ledger from this setup kit. Inspect the available Quickchat AI tools first. Prepare the Main Prompt and the two HTTP Actions using the exact field names, numeric amount type and fixed ranges. Keep log_lead_to_google_sheet as the starter name. Ask me to complete Google OAuth and Telegram Bot Token setup in the dashboard. Apply both owner/private run conditions before enabling either Action. Do not run credit-consuming tests or append expenses until I ask. Report any setting your tools cannot configure so I can complete it in the dashboard.
```


The owner completes Google consent and the Telegram connection. Review the settings and run the same checks above regardless of who entered them.


## Frequently asked questions


### How do I track expenses in Telegram with Google Sheets?


Connect a Telegram bot to a Quickchat AI Agent and authorize Google Sheets. Configure one Action to append an expense after confirmation and another to read a formula-based monthly summary. Restrict both Actions to your Telegram user ID and a private chat.


### Can the bot tell me how much I spent this month?


Yes, when the requested month and currency have a row in the configured Summary range. Google Sheets calculates the total with SUMIFS; the read Action retrieves it. An append-only Action cannot retrieve totals, and a missing summary row is not a zero.


### Can someone else read my expenses through the Telegram bot?


Both personal-data Actions must require your verified telegram_user_id and telegram_chat_type equal to private. These conditions block calls from other senders and groups. Test both cases before adding personal data, and keep access to the Sheet and Quickchat AI account restricted too.


### Is this Telegram expense tracker free?


Creating a Telegram bot is free. Quickchat AI’s Free plan supports personal, non-commercial learning with a limited AI-credit allowance. AI replies and Simulation Testing use credits; ongoing use depends on your available allowance and plan.


### Do I need Apps Script, Python or an automation server?


This recipe uses Quickchat AI Actions and a Google Sheets formula. You paste the provided request settings, JSON body and prompt into the dashboard; you do not deploy Apps Script, a Python bot or an automation server.


### Can I use my existing expense spreadsheet?


This recipe uses the spreadsheet created by the Quickchat AI Google Sheets integration. Its drive.file authorization does not give it unrestricted access to your Drive. Do not replace the spreadsheet ID with an arbitrary existing file and assume it is accessible.


### Can the bot read receipt photos or voice notes?


This tutorial covers typed expenses. Receipt extraction needs its own Telegram image-delivery and confirmation test before you rely on it. Voice transcription and PDF receipt parsing are not part of this setup.


### How does it handle different currencies and duplicate entries?


Each currency gets a separate monthly total; the recipe does not convert currencies. Confirmation reduces accidental entries but does not provide atomic duplicate prevention. If a save times out, inspect the Sheet before sending it again.
